subject: chem
title: Some Basic Concepts in Chemistry
syllabus: Matter and its nature; Dalton's atomic theory; concept of atom, molecule, element and compound; laws of chemical combination; atomic and molecular masses; mole concept; molar mass; percentage composition; empirical and molecular formulae; chemical equations and stoichiometry; limiting reagent; concentration terms: mass percent, mole fraction, molarity, molality, ppm.

body: 1 mole = 6.022 × 10^{23} particles (N_{A}). Atoms are far too small to count one by one, so we count them in moles.
n = \f{mass}{molar mass} = \f{N}{N_{A}} = \f{V (gas at STP)}{22.4 L}
Molar mass = sum of atomic masses: H_{2}O = 18, CO_{2} = 44, H_{2}SO_{4} = 98, NaCl = 58.5, glucose = 180, sucrose = 342 g mol^{−1}.
Number of ATOMS = moles of molecules × atoms per molecule. 18 g of water has 1 mol molecules but 3 mol atoms.
Equal masses of elements → the LIGHTER element has more atoms.
A balanced equation is a recipe in MOLES: 2H_{2} + O_{2} → 2H_{2}O means 2 mol + 1 mol → 2 mol.
Always convert grams → moles first, use the mole ratio, then convert back.
Limiting reagent: divide each reactant's moles by its coefficient. The SMALLEST value runs out first and decides how much product forms.
The other reactant is in excess — the left-over amount is often asked too.
For gases at STP: 1 mol = 22.4 L (some new papers use 22.7 L at 1 bar).

check.q: 4 mol H_{2} + 1 mol O_{2} → water. Limiting :

body: Molarity M = \f{mol solute}{L of solution}, Molality m = \f{mol solute}{kg of solvent}
Mass % = \f{mass solute}{mass solution} × 100; ppm = parts per million by mass; mole fraction x = \f{n_{i}}{n_{total}}.

From % and density:
M = \f{10 × d × w%}{M_{solute}}

From M and density:
m = \f{1000M}{1000d − M × M_{solute}}
Molarity changes with temperature (volume expands); molality, mass % and mole fraction do not.
Dilution: M_{1}V_{1} = M_{2}V_{2}. Neutralisation: equivalents of acid = equivalents of base.
% of an element = \f{(atoms × atomic mass)}{molar mass} × 100.
Combustion analysis: C = \f{12}{44} × mass of CO_{2};  H = \f{2}{18} × mass of H_{2}O; O by difference.
Empirical formula: % ÷ atomic mass → divide by the smallest → round (multiply by 2 or 3 if you get .5 or .33).
Molecular formula = (empirical formula) × n, where n = \f{molar mass}{empirical formula mass}.

check.q: Empirical formula CH_{2}O, M = 180. Molecular formula :

traps: Molarity uses volume of SOLUTION, molality uses mass of SOLVENT (not solution).
Count atoms, not molecules, when the question says "atoms".
Find the limiting reagent before using any product formula.
Partial pressures go by MOLES, not mass %.
A hydrate's molar mass includes its water (FeSO_{4}·7H_{2}O = 278).
Mass of product can never exceed total mass of reactants used.

steps.note: Moles, Avogadro number, molar mass and STP volume
Mole ratios and the limiting reagent
Concentration terms, empirical and molecular formulae

pyq.q: Among 10^{−9} g (each) of the following elements, which one will have the highest number of atoms? Element: Pb, Po, Pr and Pt
sol: Equal masses: number of atoms ∝ \f{1}{atomic mass}.
Pr (141) is the lightest of Pr 141, Pt 195, Pb 207, Po 209 → most atoms.

pyq.q: Number of moles and number of molecules in 1.4187 L of SO_{2} at STP respectively are
The correct order of total number of atoms present in (A) 2 moles of cyclohexane (B) 684 g of sucrose (C) 90.8 L of dihydrogen at STP is :
sol: A: C_{6}H_{12} has 18 atoms → 2 × 18 = 36 mol of atoms.
B: C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} (342 g/mol), 684 g = 2 mol × 45 atoms = 90 mol of atoms.
C: 90.8 L ÷ 22.7 L = 4 mol H_{2} → 8 mol of atoms.

pyq.q: Which of the following contain the same number of atoms? (Given : Molar mass in g mol^{−1} of H, He, O and S are 1, 4, 16 and 32 respectively) A. 2 g of O_{2} gas B. 4 g of SO_{2} gas C. 1400 mL of O_{2} at STP D. 0.05 L of He at STP E. 0.0625 mol of H_{2} gas
sol: A, C and E have the same number of atoms.

pyq.q: Match List-I (mass of substance) with List-II (number of atoms). A. 1.8 mg water B. 9.8 mg sulphuric acid C. 1.8 mg carbon D. 5.85 mg salt (NaCl) — I. 2 × 10^{−4} × N_{A} II. 1.5 × 10^{−4} × N_{A} III. 3 × 10^{−4} × N_{A} IV. 7 × 10^{−4} × N_{A}
Number of moles of methane required to produce 22 g CO_{2}(g) after combustion is x × 10^{−2} moles. The value of x is ______.
sol: CH_{4} + 2O_{2} → CO_{2} + 2H_{2}O: 1 mol CH_{4} gives 1 mol CO_{2}.

pyq.q: The number of moles of methane required to produce 11 g CO_{2}(g) after complete combustion is: (Given molar mass of methane in g mol^{−1}: 16)
The Molarity (M) of an aqueous solution containing 5.85 g of NaCl in 500 mL water is : (Given : Molar Mass Na: 23 and Cl: 35.5 g mol^{−1})
sol: M = \f{0.1}{0.5 L} = 0.2 M (taking the solution volume as 500 mL).

pyq.q: Molality (m) of 3M aqueous solution of NaCl is: (Given : Density of solution = 1.25 g mL^{−1}, Molar mass in g mol^{−1}: Na − 23, Cl − 35.5)
sol: Take 1 L: mass = 1250 g; NaCl = 3 × 58.5 = 175.5 g.

pyq.q: Density of 3 M NaCl solution is 1.25 g/mL. The molality of the solution is :
sol: 1 L of solution = 1250 g, of which NaCl = 175.5 g.

pyq.q: The density of 'x' M solution ('x' molar) of NaOH is 1.12 g mL^{−1}, while in molality, the concentration of the solution is 3 m (3 molal). Then x is (Given : Molar mass of NaOH is 40 g/mol)
Molality of an aqueous solution of urea is 4.44 m. Mole fraction of urea in solution is x × 10^{−3}. Value of x is ______ (integer answer)
sol: 4.44 mol urea per 1000 g water = 55.56 mol water.

pyq.q: A solution is prepared by adding 1 mole ethyl alcohol in 9 mole water. The mass percent of solute in the solution is ______ (Integer Answer) (Given : Molar mass in g mol^{−1} Ethyl alcohol : 46, water : 18)
sol: Mass of solute = 46 g; water = 9 × 18 = 162 g.

pyq.q: The molarity of a 70% (mass/mass) aqueous solution of a monobasic acid (X) is ______ × 10^{−1} M (Nearest integer) [Given: Density of aqueous solution of (X) is 1.25 g mL^{−1}; Molar mass of the acid is 70 g mol^{−1}]
sol: 1 L = 1250 g of solution → acid = 875 g = \f{875}{70} = 12.5 mol.

pyq.q: Concentrated nitric acid is labelled as 75% by mass. The volume in mL of the solution which contains 30 g of nitric acid is (Given : Density of nitric acid solution is 1.25 g/mL)

A solution of H_{2}SO_{4} is 31.4% H_{2}SO_{4} by mass and has a density of 1.25 g/mL. The molarity of the H_{2}SO_{4} solution is ______ M (nearest integer) [Given molar mass of H_{2}SO_{4} = 98 g mol^{−1}]
Molality of 0.8 M H_{2}SO_{4} solution (density 1.06 g cm^{−3}) is ______ × 10^{−3} m.
The molarity of 1 L orthophosphoric acid (H_{3}PO_{4}) having 70% purity by weight (specific gravity 1.54 g cm^{−3}) is ______ M. (Molar mass of H_{3}PO_{4} = 98 g mol^{−1})
The mass of sodium acetate (CH_{3}COONa) required to prepare 250 mL of 0.35 M aqueous solution is ______ g. (Molar mass of CH_{3}COONa is 82.02 g mol^{−1}) (nearest integer)

At T(K), 100 g of 98% H_{2}SO_{4} (w/w) aqueous solution is mixed with 100 g of 49% H_{2}SO_{4} (w/w) aqueous solution. What is the mole fraction of H_{2}SO_{4} in the resultant solution? (Given : Atomic mass H = 1 u; S = 32 u; O = 16 u)
What is the mole fraction of water in 10% by weight (w/w) of aqueous urea solution? [Given: Molar mass of H, O, C and N are 1, 16, 12 and 14 g mol^{−1} respectively.]
sol: 100 g: urea 10 g = 0.167 mol; water 90 g = 5 mol.

pyq.q: Given : Molar mass of C, H, O, Cl are 12, 1, 16 and 35.5 g mol^{−1}. Statement I: In 30% (w/w) solution of methanol in CCl_{4} (at T K), the mole fraction of CCl_{4} is equal to 0.33. Statement II: Mixture of methanol and CCl_{4} shows positive deviation from Raoult's law.
sol: II: methanol molecules lose some hydrogen bonding when mixed with CCl_{4} → positive deviation. TRUE.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Fortification of food with iron is done using FeSO_{4}·7H_{2}O. The mass in grams of the FeSO_{4}·7H_{2}O required to achieve 12 ppm of iron in 150 kg of wheat is ______ (Nearest integer) [Given: Molar mass of Fe, S and O respectively are 56, 32 and 16 g mol^{−1}]

Sea water, which can be considered as a 6 molar (6 M) solution of NaCl, has a density of 2 g mL^{−1}. The concentration of dissolved oxygen (O_{2}) in sea water is 5.8 ppm. Then the concentration of dissolved oxygen (O_{2}) in sea water, is x × 10^{−4} m. (nearest integer)
sol: Take 1 L = 2000 g; NaCl = 351 g → water = 1649 g.

pyq.q: At the sea level, the dry air mass percentage composition is given as nitrogen gas: 70.0, oxygen gas: 27.0 and argon gas: 3.0. If total pressure is 1.15 atm, then calculate the ratio of following respectively: (i) partial pressure of nitrogen gas to partial pressure of oxygen gas (ii) partial pressure of oxygen gas to partial pressure of argon gas (Given: Molar mass of N, O and Ar are 14, 16 and 40 g mol^{−1} respectively.)
sol: Partial pressures are in the ratio of MOLES (total pressure is not needed).

pyq.q: The quantity which changes with temperature is :
sol: Molarity uses VOLUME of solution, and volume expands with temperature.
Mass %, molality and mole fraction use only masses/moles → temperature-independent.

pyq.q: 10 mL of 2 M NaOH solution is added to 20 mL of 1 M HCl solution kept in a beaker. Now, 10 mL of this mixture is poured into a volumetric flask of 100 mL containing 2 moles of HCl and made the volume upto the mark with distilled water. The solution in this flask is :
sol: 20 mmol NaOH + 20 mmol HCl → exactly neutral NaCl; the 10 mL portion adds no acid.
Flask: 2 mol HCl in 100 mL → \f{2}{0.1} = 20 M HCl.

pyq.q: x mg of pure HCl was used to make an aqueous solution. 25.0 mL of 0.1 M Ba(OH)_{2} solution is used when the HCl solution was titrated against it. The numerical value of x is ______ × 10^{−1}. (Nearest integer) Given : Molar mass of HCl and Ba(OH)_{2} are 36.5 and 171.0 g mol^{−1} respectively.
sol: Ba(OH)_{2} = 2.5 mmol → OH^{−} = 5 mmol → HCl = 5 mmol.

pyq.q: CaCO_{3}(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl_{2}(aq) + CO_{2}(g) + H_{2}O(l). Consider the above reaction, what mass of CaCl_{2} will be formed if 250 mL of 0.76 M HCl reacts with 1000 g of CaCO_{3}? (Given : Molar mass of Ca, C, O, H and Cl are 40, 12, 16, 1 and 35.5 g mol^{−1}, respectively)
sol: HCl = 0.19 mol (limiting; 10 mol CaCO_{3} is a huge excess).

pyq.q: Mass of magnesium required to produce 220 mL of hydrogen gas at STP on reaction with excess of dil. HCl is (Given: Molar mass of Mg is 24 g mol^{−1})

Combustion of glucose (C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}) produces CO_{2} and water. The amount of oxygen (in g) required for the complete combustion of 900 g of glucose is: [Molar mass of glucose in g mol^{−1} = 180]

Butane reacts with oxygen: C_{4}H_{10}(g) + \f{13}{2}O_{2}(g) → 4CO_{2}(g) + 5H_{2}O(l). If 174.0 kg of butane is mixed with 320.0 kg of O_{2}, the volume of water formed in liters is ______. (Nearest integer) [Given : (a) Molar mass of C, H, O are 12, 1, 16 g mol^{−1} respectively, (b) Density of water = 1 g mL^{−1}]
sol: Butane = 3000 mol (needs 19500 mol O_{2}); O_{2} = 10000 mol → O_{2} is limiting.

pyq.q: The mass of iron converted into Fe_{3}O_{4} by the action of 18 g of steam is : (Given : Molar mass of H, O and Fe are 1, 16 and 56 g mol^{−1} respectively) Assume iron is present in excess :
sol: 1 mol steam reacts with \f{3}{4} mol Fe = 42 g.

pyq.q: 14.0 g of calcium metal is allowed to react with excess HCl at 1.0 atm pressure and 273 K. Which of the following statements is incorrect? [Given : Molar mass in g mol^{−1} of Ca − 40, Cl − 35.5, H − 1]
sol: Ca + 2HCl → CaCl_{2} + H_{2}; Ca = 0.35 mol (limiting, HCl in excess).
CaCl_{2} = 0.35 × 111 = 38.85 g, NOT 33.3 g → statement 3 is incorrect.
o: 0.35 mol of H_{2} gas is evolved.
7.84 L of H_{2} gas is evolved.
The limiting reagent is calcium metal.

pyq.q: For the given reaction CaCO_{3} + 2HCl → CaCl_{2} + H_{2}O + CO_{2}: if 90 g CaCO_{3} is added to 300 mL of HCl which contains 38.55% HCl by mass and has density 1.13 g mL^{−1}, then which of the following option is correct? (Given molar mass of H, Cl, Ca and O are 1, 35.5, 40 and 16 g mol^{−1} respectively.)
sol: 90 g CaCO_{3} = 0.9 mol uses 1.8 mol HCl = 65.7 g → CaCO_{3} is limiting.

pyq.q: When 81.0 g of aluminium is allowed to react with 128.0 g of oxygen gas, the mass of aluminium oxide produced in grams is ______ (Nearest integer) Given : Molar mass of Al is 27.0 g mol^{−1}; Molar mass of O is 16.0 g mol^{−1}
sol: 4Al + 3O_{2} → 2Al_{2}O_{3}. Al = 3 mol (needs 2.25 mol O_{2}); O_{2} = 4 mol → Al limiting.

pyq.q: Consider the following reaction occurring in the blast furnace: Fe_{3}O_{4}(s) + 4CO(g) → 3Fe(l) + 4CO_{2}(g). 'x' kg of iron is produced when 2.32 × 10^{3} kg Fe_{3}O_{4} and 2.8 × 10^{2} kg CO are brought together in the furnace. The value of 'x' is ______. (nearest integer) {Given: molar mass of Fe_{3}O_{4} = 232, CO = 28, Fe = 56 g mol^{−1}}
sol: Fe_{3}O_{4} = 10 kmol (needs 40 kmol CO); CO = 10 kmol → CO is limiting.

pyq.q: A + 2B → AB_{2}. 36.0 g of 'A' (Molar mass: 60 g mol^{−1}) and 56.0 g of 'B' (Molar mass: 80 g mol^{−1}) are allowed to react. Which of the following statements are correct? A. 'A' is the limiting reagent. B. 77.0 g of AB_{2} is formed. C. Molar mass of AB_{2} is 140 g mol^{−1}. D. 15.0 g of A is left unreacted after the completion of reaction.
sol: A = 0.6 mol, B = 0.7 mol. B is limiting (0.6 mol A would need 1.2 mol B) → A false.
AB_{2} = 0.35 mol × 220 = 77.0 g → B true; molar mass is 220, not 140 → C false.
A left = 0.25 mol = 15.0 g → D true.

pyq.q: How many grams of residue is obtained by heating 2.76 g of silver carbonate? (Given : Molar mass of C, O and Ag are 12, 16 and 108 g mol^{−1} respectively)
sol: Ag_{2}CO_{3} → 2Ag + CO_{2} + ½O_{2} (strong heating leaves silver metal).

pyq.q: What volume of hydrogen gas at STP would be liberated by action of 50 mL of H_{2}SO_{4} of 50% purity (density = 1.3 g mL^{−1}) on 20 g of zinc? Given : Molar mass of H, O, S, Zn are 1, 16, 32, 65 g mol^{−1} respectively.
In the reaction, 2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2Al^{3+}(aq) + 6Cl^{−}(aq) + 3H_{2}(g)
sol: Per mole HCl: ½ mol H_{2} = 11.2 L at STP ✓.
Per mole Al: 1.5 mol H_{2} = 33.6 L at STP (not 67.2 L), and gas volume always depends on T and P.
HCl(aq) is a solution — its volume is not fixed by gas laws.
o: 11.2 L H_{2}(g) at STP is produced for every mole of HCl consumed.
67.2 L H_{2}(g) at STP is produced for every mole of Al that reacts.
12 L HCl(aq) is consumed for every 6 L H_{2}(g) produced.
33.6 L H_{2}(g) is produced regardless of temperature and pressure for every mole of Al that reacts.

pyq.q: On complete combustion 1.0 g of an organic compound (X) gave 1.46 g of CO_{2} and 0.567 g of H_{2}O. The empirical formula mass of compound (X) is ______ (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} C:12, H:1, O:16)
sol: C : H : O ≈ 1 : 2 : 1 → CH_{2}O, empirical formula mass 30.

pyq.q: An organic compound weighing 500 mg, produced 220 mg of CO_{2}, on complete combustion. The percentage composition of carbon in the compound is ______ %. (nearest integer) (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} of C:12, O:16)

The ratio of mass percentage (w/w) of C : H in a hydrocarbon is 12 : 1. It has two carbon atoms. The weight (in g) of CO_{2}(g) formed when 3.38 g of this hydrocarbon is completely burnt in oxygen is : (Given : Molar mass in g mol^{−1} C:12, H:1, O:16)
sol: 12 : 1 by mass → C : H = 1 : 1 by moles → C_{2}H_{2} (26 g/mol).

pyq.q: Complete combustion of X g of an organic compound gave 0.25 g of CO_{2} and 0.12 g of H_{2}O. If the % of carbon is 25% and of hydrogen is 4.89%, then X = ______ × 10^{−3} g. (Nearest integer) (Molar mass of C, H and O are 12, 1 and 16 g mol^{−1} respectively.)
0.01 mole of an organic compound (X) containing 10% hydrogen, on complete combustion produced 0.9 g H_{2}O. Molar mass of (X) is ______ g mol^{−1}.
sol: H_{2}O = 0.05 mol → H = 0.1 mol = 0.1 g, from 0.01 mol X → 10 g H per mole.
10 g is 10% of the molar mass → M = 100 g mol^{−1}.

pyq.q: The elemental composition of a compound is 54.2% C, 9.2% H and 36.6% O. If the molar mass of the compound is 132 g mol^{−1}, the molecular formula of the compound is : [Given : The relative atomic mass of C : H : O = 12 : 1 : 16]
An oxide of iron contains 69.9% iron, its empirical formula, is: (Given : Molar mass of Fe and O are 56 and 16 g mol^{−1} respectively.)
